solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Disputes with sweetheart are not frequent

parts.note: to spar is to argue, so spars are disputes
the heart of sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: A couple's quarrels with their beloved, thankfully, are rare.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered, so something sparse is infrequent or scanty.

clue.text: Is climbing in a rough mountainous area

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the word goes upwards, so it is reversed
rough means roughed up, so the letters of in a are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is climbing in harsh, mountainous terrain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns IS into SI; 'rough' rearranges IN A into NAI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinai is the mountainous peninsula of Egypt, home of Mount Sinai.

clue.text: Charming things to wear

parts.note: sounds like attractive clothes, but means charms worn against evil

explanation.walkthrough: 'Charming' suggests attractive; here it means acting as a charm.
explanation.definitionFit: These are protective trinkets or talismans worn to ward off harm.

clue.text: The point of this device is not always apparent

definitions.text: The point of this device is not always apparent

parts.words: The point of this device is not always apparent
parts.note: sounds like a puzzling gadget, but the sharp point is literally hidden by a clasp

explanation.walkthrough: 'point' seems to mean purpose; it is the literal sharp tip, tucked into a guard.
explanation.definitionFit: This fastener has its pin tip enclosed in a clasp so it cannot prick.

clue.text: Shades of Ibsen

definitions.meaning: first meaning: shades are spirits of the dead, phantoms
second meaning: the title of a play by Henrik Ibsen

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase it suggests shades of meaning in Ibsen's work; it is two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Shades are spectres of the dead, and Ghosts is the title of Ibsen's 1881 drama.

clue.text: Draw a hole

parts.note: sounds like sketching a hole, but in golf means tying a hole with an opponent

explanation.walkthrough: In match-play golf, players who take the same strokes on a hole are said to share or split it.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers say they split a hole equally when each takes the same score on it.

clue.text: Power at mains switch

indicators.note: to switch is to swap around, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Electrical power is controlled at the mains switch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power' and 'mains switch' suggest electricity; the power is bodily endurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the strength to keep going.

clue.text: Deep breath?

parts.note: deep is a poetic word for the ocean, so a breath from it is a wind off the water

explanation.walkthrough: 'the deep' is the sea, so its breath is a wind coming off the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A light wind blowing from the ocean onto land is the deep's breath.

clue.text: Swallows what's flung out in two directions

indicators.note: the shuffled word sits in between the two compass letters

parts.note: E and S, east and south on the compass

indicators.note: flung out suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Something swallowed is then hurled back out every which way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's' is a link; 'in two directions' reads as scattering everywhere, but means two compass letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To engulf is to swallow up or overwhelm completely.

clue.text: Girl able to recall where dates can be found

parts.note: Alma is a girl's name

indicators.note: recall read as calling back, so the word is turned round

parts.note: to be able is to be capable, so can

explanation.surface: A woman who can remember where and when things happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dates' suggests romantic outings or fruit; here they are calendar dates.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a calendar-based annual listing dates, tides and events.

clue.text: It affects the weather in a winter battle zone

parts.note: winter is the cold season, so cold stands for it
the front is where the fighting happens in a war

explanation.surface: Weather conditions shape a winter military campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winter' is used adjectivally for cold, and the battle zone is the front.
explanation.definitionFit: This leading edge of a cool air mass brings rain and a drop in temperature.

clue.text: Cook sent in more soup

indicators.note: to cook something is to tamper with it, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An order to a kitchen: the cook sent in more soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' seems to be a person but is the signal to rearrange SENT IN MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Minestrone is a thick Italian vegetable broth with pasta or rice.

clue.text: Anger about one point in the matter

indicators.note: the anger word goes around the single compass letter

parts.note: ire is anger
N, north, one point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone's anger concerns a single point in the affair under discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used in letters and law meaning concerning or regarding the matter.

clue.text: Story-teller for soap set around English capital

indicators.note: the reordered letters go around the English letter
set means arranged in a new way, so the letters of soap are reordered
the capital, or head, of English is its first letter

explanation.surface: A writer working for a TV soap opera set in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges SOAP into ASOP, and 'around' wraps it round E, the 'capital' of English.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek author of fables, a famous teller of moral tales.

clue.text: Gave up and left

definitions.meaning: first meaning: renounced or gave up on, a verb in the past tense
second meaning: deserted, as in left behind

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses use the same past form: having given up and having deserted.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon is to relinquish a plan or to desert a place or person.

clue.text: In poor health and expired taking the waters

indicators.note: the dying word takes in the waters, holding them inside

parts.note: to expire is to die, so died
seas are waters

explanation.surface: Someone in poor health took a water cure but died anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Diseased means affected by illness, sick or unhealthy.

clue.text: Upset friends, content to be casual

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: pals are friends
content means happy

explanation.surface: Annoyed friends are told to be content with a relaxed attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' rearranges PALS into SLAP, followed by HAPPY.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaphappy means cheerfully careless or haphazard, an easygoing irresponsible manner.

clue.text: A good one can always grow better

definitions.text: A good one can always grow better

parts.words: A good one can always grow better
parts.note: reads as a motto about self-improvement, but a skilled cultivator literally raises plants better

explanation.walkthrough: 'grow better' seems to mean improve oneself; it means raise better plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilful horticulturist produces finer flowers and vegetables than an amateur.

clue.text: China ends red revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political headline: China brings its Communist revolution to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; it is porcelain. Dresden china is fine porcelain from Meissen, near Dresden.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden is a name for fine German porcelain, a type of china.

clue.text: A tissue of lies divides the church

indicators.note: a tissue is woven, so the letters of lies are woven into a new order

explanation.surface: A web of falsehood causes a split in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divides the church' hints at schism; it is the passage dividing the pews.
explanation.definitionFit: The aisle is the passage running down a church, separating the rows of pews.

clue.text: It is highly important to change lanes entering M1

indicators.note: the motorway letters go into the rearranged word
to change lanes is to switch, so the letters of lanes are rearranged

parts.note: M1 read as M and I, with the figure 1 as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A driving instructor stresses that changing lanes on the M1 is vital.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; its figure 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Seminal means highly influential, of foundational importance.

clue.text: Out of work, one gets led astray

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: led astray means taken off course, so the letters wander into another order

explanation.surface: An unemployed person falls into bad company.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can mean unemployed or not working, as of workers laid off.

clue.text: The sweet nonsense of moneymaking

parts.note: the Mint is where money is made
humbug is nonsense or sham

explanation.surface: A cynic dismissing the cosy idea of earning money as a sweet affair.
explanation.walkthrough: A mint humbug is a British boiled sweet flavoured with peppermint, often striped.
explanation.definitionFit: This striped peppermint confection is a type of hard candy.

clue.text: Heaven-sent sustenance for many a girl

parts.note: M, a thousand in Roman numerals, stands for many
Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Food from heaven to feed many a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Exodus, the Israelites were fed bread from heaven in the wilderness.

clue.text: Tip in stupendous style

indicators.note: the answer lies in the letters of stupendous

explanation.surface: Tipping a waiter generously, in great style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' seems to be a gratuity; it means overturn.
explanation.definitionFit: To up-end something is to turn it over or tip it on its end.

clue.text: Annoyed when out — of painkiller?

indicators.note: when out suggests things are disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone irritated after running out of pain relief.
explanation.definitionFit: An anodyne is a medicine that soothes or relieves pain.

clue.text: Wood found where one river enters another

indicators.note: one river's name goes into the other's

parts.note: the Spey is a river in Scotland
the Inn is a river in Austria and Bavaria

explanation.surface: A wooded spot found at a river confluence.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inn flows through Austria and Bavaria; the Spey is a Scottish salmon river.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinney is a small copse or thicket of trees.

clue.text: An idle form of rejection

indicators.note: a form of the letters means a different shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lazy refusal is described as a kind of rejection.
explanation.definitionFit: Denial is refusal to accept or grant something, a way of rejecting it.

clue.text: Optical shutter

parts.note: sounds like part of a camera, but describes the flap of skin that closes over the eye

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests photographic equipment; the shutter is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin fold that closes over the eye works like a camera's shutter.
